reviews.title: No Female Models!
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app since 2018, and I’ve never had a problem with the paid features implemented. It helped me a lot with understanding poses and anatomy, and I think it’s the easiest posing software to use you could ask for. Until today, when I open the app and discover that I can only use the single male model without signing up for a trial. Believe it or not, I was NOT trying to draw a man. I was able to recover my old account, which provided me with the female models I was looking for, but if I had been a newer user I would’ve had to pay up. I really don’t like the idea of women being some sort of DLC thing- I see enough of that in the real world! I understand that these kinds of cuts are necessary for making the app profitable, but this feels exclusionary. CSP has all of its posing features on its free version, I’d recommend that for any artists interested in something more diverse.

reviews.title: Long-time user no longer a fan
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app way back when the whole thing was pretty bare bones (maybe 5-6 years ago?) and I’ve watched it grow and expand into a really great resource for art references. But sadly I’ve also seen it really regress in certain areas to the point where I really can’t rely on it anymore. 

For reference, I have the pro version because I think developers should get paid for good work. I’ve also bought a weapon prop pack in the past because I didn’t mind paying to have more props. But then they added a subscription, and suddenly some of my previously paid-for props disappeared (bows and arrows and a dagger, to name a few) and new ones were available only to monthly subscribers.

You have every right to add new features and charge whatever you want for them. But removing things people paid to access previously crosses a line, and I can’t trust a tool to be part of a creative pipeline without it having some consistency I can depend on.
